name: The Fool
shortMeaning: A new journey begins with open heart and fearless spirit, trusting the universe to catch you.
reversedMeaning: Reckless leaps without looking risk leading you off the cliff of your own making.

rws.scene: A youth in embroidered clothes steps toward a cliff edge, a white rose in one hand and a small bundle on a stick over the shoulder, a little white dog leaping at the heels, sun blazing behind.
symbols: the unseen cliff edge — the risk he has not yet looked down at
the white rose — innocence, wanting nothing in particular
the small dog — instinct, barking a warning he may or may not heed

name: The Magician
shortMeaning: You have all the tools you need — channel your will to transform intention into reality.
reversedMeaning: Potential sits unused or is being twisted toward manipulation and self-deception.

rws.scene: A figure stands at a table bearing wand, cup, sword and pentacle, one arm raised to the sky holding a wand and the other pointing to the ground, an infinity sign above the head, roses and lilies around.
symbols: as above, so below — channelling something larger into an actual act
all four suits on the table — every tool is already available
the lemniscate — power that renews as long as it keeps moving

name: The High Priestess
shortMeaning: The answers you seek dwell in silence — trust your deep inner knowing over surface logic.
reversedMeaning: Secrets withheld or intuition suppressed create a fog that distorts your path forward.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Priestess of the Silver Star

rws.scene: A veiled woman sits between a black pillar and a white one, a crescent moon at her feet, a scroll marked TORA half-hidden in her lap, a pomegranate curtain behind her.
symbols: the curtain — what she knows is behind her, not spoken
the half-hidden scroll — knowledge withheld until you are ready
the two pillars — she sits at the threshold, not on either side

name: The Empress
shortMeaning: Lush abundance flows when you honor your creative power and nurture what you love.
reversedMeaning: Creative stagnation or over-nurturing others at the expense of your own flourishing.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Daughter of the Mighty Ones

rws.scene: A woman reclines on cushions in a field of ripening wheat, a stream and forest behind, a crown of twelve stars on her head and a heart-shaped shield bearing Venus at her side.
symbols: the ripe wheat — something is already growing and needs no forcing
the flowing stream — pleasure, fertility, ease
cushions rather than a stone throne — authority through abundance, not force

name: The Emperor
shortMeaning: Establish firm foundations and assert your authority to build lasting order and security.
reversedMeaning: Rigid control or abused authority creates oppressive structures that stifle growth.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Son of the Morning, Chief among the Mighty

rws.scene: A stern bearded man sits on a stone throne carved with rams' heads, an ankh sceptre in hand, armour showing beneath his red robe, barren mountains behind.
symbols: the stone throne — order that does not move for feelings
the barren mountains — the cost of a life built on structure
armour under the robe — always braced, never quite at rest

name: The Hierophant
shortMeaning: Seek wisdom through established traditions, spiritual mentors, or sacred community.
reversedMeaning: Breaking free from dogma invites authentic spiritual discovery outside conventional boundaries.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Magus of the Eternal Gods

rws.scene: A robed teacher sits between two pillars wearing a triple crown, one hand raised in blessing, two tonsured acolytes kneeling before him, crossed keys at his feet.
symbols: the crossed keys — access granted through an institution, not found alone
the two kneeling students — knowledge passed down a line
the raised hand — sanction, permission, orthodoxy

name: The Lovers
shortMeaning: A profound choice or deep union calls you to align your values with your heart's truth.
reversedMeaning: Misaligned values create discord in relationships and lead to choices you may regret.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Children of the Voice, the Oracle of the Mighty Gods

rws.scene: A naked man and woman stand beneath a great winged angel in a blazing sun; behind her a serpent coils in a fruit tree, behind him a tree of flames, a mountain rising between them.
symbols: the angel above — the choice is being witnessed by something larger
the two trees — desire on one side, will on the other
the man looks at her, she looks up — they are not facing the same way

name: The Chariot
shortMeaning: Harness opposing forces with iron will and charge forward toward triumphant victory.
reversedMeaning: Without direction or self-control, conflicting impulses scatter your momentum and derail success.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Child of the Power of the Waters, Lord of the Triumph of Light

rws.scene: An armoured figure stands in a chariot drawn by one black sphinx and one white, a canopy of stars overhead, a walled city behind, crescent moons on the shoulders.
symbols: black and white sphinxes — opposing drives yoked to one direction
no reins in his hands — control held by will, not by force
the city behind — he has already left safety

name: Strength
shortMeaning: True power comes not from force but from gentle courage and compassionate self-mastery.
reversedMeaning: Self-doubt and unmastered emotions reveal themselves as the real obstacle to overcome.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Daughter of the Flaming Sword, Leader of the Lion

rws.scene: A woman in white calmly closes her hands on a lion's jaws, an infinity sign above her head, a garland of flowers looping between them.
symbols: hands on the jaws, not a weapon — mastery by patience
the flower garland — the beast is led, not beaten
the lion leans in — the wild part is not the enemy

name: The Hermit
shortMeaning: Step back from the noise of the world to find the lantern of wisdom that lights your path.
reversedMeaning: Excessive isolation becomes a prison rather than a sanctuary for genuine self-discovery.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Prophet of the Eternal, the Magus of the Voice of Light

rws.scene: An old man in a grey hood stands alone on a snowy peak, holding up a lantern containing a six-pointed star, a staff in his other hand.
symbols: the lantern — a light small enough for one person only
the snowy summit — the isolation the search costs
the staff — this is a chosen walk, not exile

name: Wheel of Fortune
shortMeaning: The wheel turns and fortune shifts — embrace the cycles of change as the universe realigns.
reversedMeaning: Resisting inevitable change keeps the wheel stuck, prolonging the difficult phase unnecessarily.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Lord of the Forces of Life

rws.scene: A great wheel marked with letters and alchemical signs turns in the sky; a sphinx with a sword sits on top, a serpent slides down one side, a jackal-headed figure rises on the other, four winged creatures read books in the corners.
symbols: the turning wheel — the moment is moving whether you act or not
rising and falling figures — no position on the wheel is permanent
the still sphinx at the top — the centre is the only steady place

name: Justice
shortMeaning: Truth prevails and every action meets its consequence — stand in integrity and trust the scales.
reversedMeaning: Dishonesty or avoided accountability creates karmic imbalance that will demand correction.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Daughter of the Lords of Truth, Ruler of the Balance

rws.scene: A crowned figure sits between two pillars, an upright sword in the right hand and level scales in the left, a purple veil behind.
symbols: the raised sword — a decision will be made and it will cut
the level scales — consequence measured, not forgiven
the veil behind — the whole picture is not visible to you

name: The Hanged Man
shortMeaning: Willingly pausing and surrendering control reveals the profound wisdom that comes from new angles.
reversedMeaning: Unnecessary delays or martyrdom trap you in suspension without the enlightenment it was meant to bring.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Spirit of the Mighty Waters

rws.scene: A man hangs upside down by one ankle from a living T-shaped tree, his free leg crossed behind, hands behind his back, a halo of light around his calm face.
symbols: hanging by choice — the rope is not a trap, he arranged it
the halo — the reward of the reversed view is insight
the crossed leg — stillness held deliberately, not collapse

name: Death
shortMeaning: What must end will end — release the old with grace so the new can be magnificently born.
reversedMeaning: Clinging to what is already dead prevents the beautiful transformation waiting on the other side.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Child of the Great Transformers, Lord of the Gates of Death

rws.scene: A skeleton in black armour rides a white horse carrying a black banner with a white rose; a king lies dead, a bishop pleads, a maiden turns away, a child kneels; a sun rises between two towers in the distance.
symbols: the white rose on a black flag — an ending that is also clean
the king already fallen — status does not exempt anyone
the sunrise beyond — this is a passage, not the end of the road

name: Temperance
shortMeaning: Patient alchemy blends opposites into perfect harmony, revealing your highest integrated purpose.
reversedMeaning: Excess and imbalance disrupt the sacred flow that keeps mind, body, and spirit in alignment.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Daughter of the Reconcilers, Bringer-forth of Life

rws.scene: A winged figure stands with one foot on land and one in a stream, pouring liquid between two cups, a path behind leading to mountains and a crown of light.
symbols: one foot in water, one on land — holding two natures at once
liquid crossing between cups — nothing is lost, only recombined
the far path — this is a long moderation, not a quick fix

name: The Devil
shortMeaning: The chains that bind you are of your own making — shadow work and honest confrontation bring freedom.
reversedMeaning: Liberation from toxic patterns becomes possible when you acknowledge the chains you've forged yourself.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Lord of the Gates of Matter, Child of the Forces of Time

rws.scene: A horned goat-headed figure crouches on a pedestal, one hand raised, an inverted star on its brow; a naked man and woman stand chained at the neck, small horns growing, tails begun.
symbols: the loose chains — they could lift them off and do not
the growing horns — you begin to resemble what you serve
the raised hand — a mock blessing, a bargain that looks like permission

name: The Tower
shortMeaning: Sudden upheaval shatters false foundations — the destruction clears the way for authentic rebuilding.
reversedMeaning: Resisting inevitable collapse only prolongs the crisis and delays the freedom waiting beyond it.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty

rws.scene: Lightning strikes a tall tower on a crag, blasting the crown off its top; flames burst from the windows and two figures fall headlong through the air.
symbols: the crown blown off — what falls first is the false authority
falling headfirst — no dignified way down
the lightning from outside — this came from beyond your control

name: The Star
shortMeaning: After the storm, the stars emerge to pour healing light and renewed hope upon your path.
reversedMeaning: Lost faith and despair dim the starlight — reconnecting with hope requires gentle self-compassion.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Daughter of the Firmament, Dweller between the Waters

rws.scene: A naked woman kneels at a pool, one foot on the water and one on land, pouring from two jugs — one into the pool, one onto the earth; one great eight-pointed star and seven smaller ones shine overhead, an ibis in a tree.
symbols: completely unclothed — nothing left to defend after the Tower
water returned to both pool and land — giving back without calculating
the great star — quiet guidance, visible only once it is dark

name: The Moon
shortMeaning: The moonlit path through illusion and fear leads to profound truths hidden in the unconscious depths.
reversedMeaning: As the fog of confusion lifts, repressed fears and illusions are finally ready to be released.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Ruler of Flux and Reflux, Child of the Sons of the Mighty

rws.scene: A moon with a downturned face sheds drops of light; a dog and a wolf howl below, a crayfish crawls from a pool, and a path runs between two towers toward far hills.
symbols: dog and wolf — the tame and the wild fear of the same thing
the crayfish emerging — something old surfacing from the deep
the path between the towers — you can walk it, but not see the end

name: The Sun
shortMeaning: Radiant success, joy, and clarity illuminate your life as the sun shines its full warmth upon you.
reversedMeaning: When inner clouds block the sun's rays, joy becomes elusive and success feels just out of reach.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Lord of the Fire of the World

rws.scene: A naked child rides a white horse holding a great red banner, beneath a huge radiant sun with a face; four sunflowers lean over a wall behind.
symbols: the child unguarded — nothing hidden, nothing performed
the banner held loosely — joy that needs no grip
the wall behind — the garden is left, the open ground taken

name: Judgement
shortMeaning: A divine awakening calls you to rise, embrace your highest calling, and leave the past behind.
reversedMeaning: Harsh self-judgment or refusing the inner call keeps you buried when it's time to rise and be reborn.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Spirit of the Primal Fire

rws.scene: An angel blows a trumpet hung with a cross-marked banner; grey figures — a man, a woman, a child — rise from open coffins on the water, arms lifted, mountains behind.
symbols: rising from the coffins — the past is being answered for, not buried
arms open, not defensive — the reckoning is welcomed
the trumpet — the call comes from outside; the timing is not yours

name: The World
shortMeaning: A great cycle reaches glorious completion — you stand whole, accomplished, and ready for what's next.
reversedMeaning: Unfinished business or shortcuts taken prevent the full experience of hard-won completion and joy.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: The Great One of the Night of Time

rws.scene: A figure draped in a violet scarf dances inside a laurel wreath holding two wands, with an angel, an eagle, a bull and a lion in the four corners.
symbols: the closed wreath — a full circuit, genuinely completed
two wands, balanced — the Magician's single wand now doubled and mastered
the four creatures — every element accounted for

name: Ace of Wands
shortMeaning: A spark of divine inspiration arrives — seize this creative potential and act with bold passion.
reversedMeaning: Creative blocks or squandered inspiration leave potential untapped and momentum lost.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: Root of the Powers of Fire

rws.scene: A hand emerges from a cloud gripping a sprouting wand, loose leaves falling, a castle on a distant hill.
symbols: the sprouting leaves — raw life already breaking out of the wood
the hand from the cloud — an offer, not yet a decision
the distant castle — where this could go, still far off

name: Two of Wands
shortMeaning: Survey the world before you from your tower of achievement and plan your next bold expansion.
reversedMeaning: Fear of venturing beyond the familiar keeps you surveying horizons you never dare to reach.

rws.scene: A man in red stands on a castle battlement holding a small globe, one wand fixed to the wall and one in his hand, looking out over sea and land.
symbols: the globe in his hand — the world considered, not yet travelled
one wand bolted down, one held — half committed, half free
standing inside the walls — planning from safety

name: Three of Wands
shortMeaning: Ships return laden with promise — your initial efforts bear fruit as new opportunities approach.
reversedMeaning: Frustrating delays and obstacles block the anticipated returns on your earlier investments.

rws.scene: A figure stands on a cliff with his back to us, three wands planted around him, watching ships sail out across the water.
symbols: his back turned — the decision is behind him now
ships already leaving — what was set in motion is under way
the high vantage — waiting with a wide view, not idly

name: Four of Wands
shortMeaning: Celebrate this joyful milestone surrounded by those who love you — a moment of pure communal harmony.
reversedMeaning: Joy celebrated alone or amid unstable foundations lacks the communal warmth it truly deserves.

rws.scene: Two figures raise bouquets beneath a flowered garland strung between four upright wands, a castle and a crowd behind.
symbols: the garland between four wands — a threshold you pass through together
raised bouquets — celebration that is shared, not private
the castle behind — arrival somewhere stable

name: Five of Wands
shortMeaning: Competing energies and differing views create friction — channel this into productive challenge.
reversedMeaning: Avoided conflict festers into internal tension, or a long dispute finally finds resolution.

rws.scene: Five youths swing wands at each other in a disordered scuffle, none clearly winning, no one hurt.
symbols: no one is bleeding — friction, not real war
all five wands at different angles — nobody is coordinated
open ground — this is a scramble for position

name: Six of Wands
shortMeaning: You ride triumphant into a well-earned victory — let the crowd's recognition fuel your confidence.
reversedMeaning: Success tainted by ego or a victory met with silence rather than the recognition you deserved.

rws.scene: A rider crowned with laurel sits on a white horse, a wreath tied to his wand, a crowd of walkers accompanying him.
symbols: the laurel wreath — public recognition, formally given
the crowd on foot — his win is witnessed and carried by others
riding, not fighting — the contest is already over

name: Seven of Wands
shortMeaning: Hold your ground against all challengers — your position is worth defending with fierce conviction.
reversedMeaning: Feeling overwhelmed by opposition makes you consider abandoning the position you've worked hard to hold.

rws.scene: A man on high ground strikes downward against six wands rising at him from below, wearing mismatched boots.
symbols: the high ground — he has the advantage as long as he holds it
six against one — the pressure is real and outnumbering
mismatched boots — he was not fully ready when this began

name: Eight of Wands
shortMeaning: Everything accelerates as wands fly in rapid succession — expect swift news, travel, or rapid change.
reversedMeaning: What should be swift is frustratingly stalled — internal misalignment slows the needed momentum.

rws.scene: Eight wands fly in parallel through clear sky above a river and green hills, with no figure anywhere.
symbols: no people at all — this is momentum, not somebody's effort
all eight parallel — everything moving one way at last
descending toward land — arrival is near

name: Nine of Wands
shortMeaning: Battered but standing, you guard what you have built — one more effort will see you through.
reversedMeaning: Battle-weary and borderline paranoid, the last reserves of resilience threaten to give way.

rws.scene: A bandaged man leans on one wand, eight more standing behind him like a fence, watching warily off-frame.
symbols: the head bandage — he has already been hurt once
eight wands as a fence — what he has defended so far
still standing — worn down but not beaten

name: Ten of Wands
shortMeaning: You carry a heavy load toward the finish line — the burden is real, but the destination is close.
reversedMeaning: Burned out under an unbearable burden, you must learn to delegate and put down what isn't yours to carry.

rws.scene: A man bends under an armful of ten wands, face hidden by the load, carrying them toward a house in the distance.
symbols: the bundle blocking his view — the load has replaced the goal
the house ahead — the end is close, which is why he will not put it down
carrying all ten alone — none of it delegated

name: Page of Wands
shortMeaning: The world ignites with possibility — pursue every spark of curiosity with fearless youthful energy.
reversedMeaning: Bright enthusiasm without direction scatters into a trail of unfinished projects and distractions.

rws.scene: A youth in a patterned tunic stands holding a tall wand, looking up at its tip, pyramids and desert behind.
symbols: looking up at the wand — curiosity before capability
the desert — nothing built here yet
feet planted, wand still — a message received, not yet acted on

name: Knight of Wands
shortMeaning: Charge into your passion with the fearless speed of a knight who has never met an obstacle worth fearing.
reversedMeaning: Reckless haste and scattered fire burn bright but short, leaving a trail of incomplete ambitions.

rws.scene: An armoured knight on a rearing horse charges forward, plumed helmet, salamanders on his tunic, pyramids behind.
symbols: the rearing horse — more force than direction
salamanders — fire that survives its own burning
armour and haste together — bold, and not looking far ahead

name: Queen of Wands
shortMeaning: Radiant and self-assured, you draw others into your magnetic orbit with warmth and bold creative fire.
reversedMeaning: Insecurity masquerading as confidence becomes demanding and jealous, alienating those you need.

rws.scene: A crowned queen sits facing outward on a throne carved with lions, a wand in one hand and a sunflower in the other, a black cat at her feet.
symbols: the sunflower — warmth that turns toward what it wants
the black cat — instinct and shadow kept close, not denied
facing straight out — nothing hidden about her

name: King of Wands
shortMeaning: Visionary leadership and entrepreneurial fire inspire others to follow your bold, courageous example.
reversedMeaning: Unchecked fire becomes domineering and reckless, burning allies with impulsive, authoritarian decisions.

rws.scene: A crowned king sits at an angle on a throne of lions and salamanders, wand in hand, a live salamander at his feet.
symbols: seated at an angle — already half turned toward action
the living salamander — vision that has become real
the wand held upright — authority in what he creates

name: Ace of Cups
shortMeaning: A cup overflows with divine love and emotional possibility — open your heart to receive this gift.
reversedMeaning: An overflowing cup turned upside down spills the gift of love before it can be received.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: Root of the Powers of Water

rws.scene: A hand from a cloud offers a cup overflowing in five streams, a dove descending with a wafer, lotuses on the water below.
symbols: five overflowing streams — more feeling than the vessel can hold
the descending dove — the offer comes from above, unearned
open water beneath — where it will all end up

name: Two of Cups
shortMeaning: Two souls meet in perfect mutual recognition — a partnership built on genuine connection and love.
reversedMeaning: What was once harmonious union shows cracks of disconnection and growing imbalance.

rws.scene: A man and a woman face each other exchanging cups, a winged lion's head above a staff of entwined serpents rising between them.
symbols: cups exchanged, not taken — an equal trade
the caduceus between them — healing through the meeting itself
standing on level ground — neither one above

name: Three of Cups
shortMeaning: Raise a cup with cherished friends — joy multiplies when shared in beloved community.
reversedMeaning: Celebration turns sour through overindulgence, gossip, or exclusionary cliques and shallow friendships.

rws.scene: Three women raise their cups together in a circle, dancing among fruit and vines.
symbols: cups raised to touch — joy that requires other people
the harvest underfoot — celebrating something actually gathered
a closed circle — belonging, with an inside and an outside

name: Four of Cups
shortMeaning: In meditative discontent, you fail to notice the new cup the universe quietly extends toward you.
reversedMeaning: Eyes finally open, you notice the gift being offered and choose renewed engagement over apathy.

rws.scene: A young man sits under a tree with folded arms, three cups on the grass before him, a fourth offered from a cloud that he does not look at.
symbols: folded arms — refusal before consideration
the unnoticed fourth cup — a real offer, missed by inattention
seated under the tree — withdrawn into himself

name: Five of Cups
shortMeaning: Grief over what was spilled may prevent you from seeing the two cups still standing behind you.
reversedMeaning: After sitting with loss, you find the courage to turn around and embrace what still remains.

rws.scene: A figure in a black cloak looks down at three spilled cups, two still standing behind, a bridge leading to a castle across the river.
symbols: three spilled, two upright — the loss is real but not total
the cloak turned inward — grief that has not looked up
the bridge already there — the way back exists whenever he turns

name: Six of Cups
shortMeaning: Sweet nostalgia and innocent joy return as a gift from the past that nourishes the present.
reversedMeaning: Rose-tinted memories keep you anchored in the past, unable to fully inhabit your present life.

rws.scene: A child hands another child a cup filled with white flowers in a village courtyard, five more flowered cups around them.
symbols: flowers growing in the cups — the past kept alive and tended
two children — innocence, or the memory of it
the courtyard walls — a safe enclosure, and a small one

name: Seven of Cups
shortMeaning: Amid the fog of fantasy and endless possibility, one cup holds real treasure — discern wisely.
reversedMeaning: The dreamy fog lifts, bringing clarity that cuts through illusion to reveal which choice is truly real.

rws.scene: A dark silhouette faces seven cups floating in cloud, each holding something different: a face, a veiled figure, a snake, a castle, jewels, a wreath, a dragon.
symbols: all seven in cloud — none of it is solid yet
the veiled figure — the most attractive option is the least examined
the figure only a silhouette — he has not committed enough to be real

name: Eight of Cups
shortMeaning: You turn your back on what once satisfied you, following the moon's pull toward deeper meaning.
reversedMeaning: Fear of leaving what no longer serves you keeps you wandering without the courage to truly depart.

rws.scene: A cloaked man walks away over rough ground toward mountains, eight cups stacked neatly behind him, the moon in eclipse above.
symbols: the cups left standing and undamaged — he leaves something that still works
his back to us — the choice is not up for discussion
the eclipsed moon — leaving at a time that feels unfinished

name: Nine of Cups
shortMeaning: The wish card grants your heart's desire — sit in the contentment of emotional abundance fulfilled.
reversedMeaning: Material satisfaction without inner fulfillment proves hollow, and greed for more replaces gratitude.

rws.scene: A well-fed man in a red cap sits with folded arms before a curved counter draped in blue, nine cups arranged in a row behind him.
symbols: the cups behind, not shared — satisfaction kept for himself
folded arms — content, and a little closed
one row, evenly spaced — the wish granted, tidily

name: Ten of Cups
shortMeaning: A rainbow of divine love crowns the scene of lasting family harmony and shared emotional fulfillment.
reversedMeaning: The picture-perfect family vision hides cracks of dysfunction and values that have drifted apart.

rws.scene: A couple stand with arms raised beneath a rainbow of ten cups, two children dancing beside them, a house and river behind.
symbols: the rainbow — a promise after weather, not instead of it
arms open, not holding the cups — the joy is not gripped
children dancing apart — happiness that does not need supervising

name: Page of Cups
shortMeaning: A fish leaps from a cup with a message — approach life with childlike wonder and open-hearted intuition.
reversedMeaning: Emotional immaturity or escapist fantasies block the creative and intuitive gifts waiting to emerge.

rws.scene: A youth in a flowered tunic holds up a cup from which a fish is rising to look at him, a wavy sea behind.
symbols: the fish in the cup — the unconscious speaking up unexpectedly
the absurd made welcome — he is amused, not alarmed
flowered clothes against a rough sea — softness in a moving element

name: Knight of Cups
shortMeaning: The romantic knight arrives bearing a cup of dreams — follow your heart's most idealistic vision.
reversedMeaning: Dreamy idealism ungrounded in reality leads to moody disappointment when fantasy meets truth.

rws.scene: A knight in winged helmet rides a white horse at a walk, holding a cup out steadily before him, a stream ahead.
symbols: riding at a walk — the only knight who does not rush
winged helmet and heels — imagination, moving deliberately
the cup held level — an offer carried without spilling

name: Queen of Cups
shortMeaning: Deeply empathic and intuitively wise, you hold space for others while maintaining your own emotional depth.
reversedMeaning: Emotional boundaries dissolve into co-dependency or emotional manipulation disguised as care.

rws.scene: A queen sits on a throne at the water's edge, absorbed in an ornate closed cup shaped like a shrine.
symbols: the lidded cup — the only cup in the deck that is closed
her throne on the shoreline — between feeling and solid ground
her whole attention inward — she reads by feeling first

name: King of Cups
shortMeaning: Mastery of emotion allows compassionate wisdom to flow — lead from the heart with serene authority.
reversedMeaning: Emotional repression bubbles into manipulation or volatile outbursts that undermine trust and wisdom.

rws.scene: A king sits on a throne floating on choppy sea, a cup in one hand and a sceptre in the other, a fish leaping and a ship riding the swell behind.
symbols: a throne on open water — steadiness held over unsteady depths
the fish and the ship — emotion and enterprise both in motion
dry robes on a rough sea — feeling deeply without being swamped

name: Ace of Swords
shortMeaning: A sword of truth cuts through confusion — mental clarity arrives with stunning, liberating precision.
reversedMeaning: The sword of clarity is blunted by confusion, leaving you mired in misinformation and mental fog.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: Root of the Powers of Air

rws.scene: A hand from a cloud grips an upright sword crowned with a laurel wreath and a palm, six drops of light falling, barren peaks below.
symbols: the crowned sword — clarity that arrives like a verdict
the barren mountains — truth does not care whether it is comfortable
held point-up — a decision waiting to be brought down

name: Two of Swords
shortMeaning: Blindfolded at the crossroads, you must make a decision without perfect information — trust your gut.
reversedMeaning: Paralyzed between impossible options, avoidance of the truth only prolongs the painful stalemate.

rws.scene: A blindfolded woman sits on a stone bench before a moonlit sea, two swords crossed over her chest in perfect balance.
symbols: the blindfold — she has chosen not to look at the choice
the two swords crossed over the heart — the stalemate is held by effort
the sea at her back — the feelings she has turned away from

name: Three of Swords
shortMeaning: Three swords pierce the heart — pain, grief, and truth arrive together in a storm of necessary clarity.
reversedMeaning: After the storm of heartbreak, healing gently begins as you remove the swords one painful step at a time.

rws.scene: Three swords pierce a red heart suspended in grey rain and cloud, with no figure present.
symbols: no person in the image — the pain is the whole picture
rain behind — grief that is weather, not permanent climate
the heart still whole around the blades — pierced, not destroyed

name: Four of Swords
shortMeaning: Step away from the battlefield — this sacred pause of rest and reflection will restore your strength.
reversedMeaning: Restlessness prevents the rest that is desperately needed, driving you toward the edge of burnout.

rws.scene: A knight lies in stone effigy on a tomb inside a church, hands pressed in prayer, three swords hanging on the wall and one lying beneath him, a stained-glass window above.
symbols: lying down, not dead — retreat chosen on purpose
three swords stowed on the wall — the fight put away, not lost
the window's light — recovery in a protected place

name: Five of Swords
shortMeaning: A hollow victory gathered at great cost — not every battle won is worth the allies lost in the fight.
reversedMeaning: Old wounds and conflicts finally open to the possibility of reconciliation and genuine forgiveness.

rws.scene: A smirking man gathers up swords while two defeated figures walk away with their backs turned, under a ragged sky.
symbols: he collects the swords — a win that leaves him holding everything
the two walking away — what the victory cost in company
the torn clouds — the air has not cleared

name: Six of Swords
shortMeaning: Cross through the turbulent waters toward calmer shores — this journey is necessary and you will arrive.
reversedMeaning: Carrying unresolved baggage makes the passage rougher — old wounds reopen before they can heal.

rws.scene: A ferryman poles a boat carrying a cloaked woman and child, six swords standing upright in the hull, choppy water on one side and calm on the other.
symbols: the swords carried, not discarded — the trouble comes along
rough water beside still water — moving out of turbulence mid-crossing
the passengers hooded and quiet — leaving is not the same as being over it

name: Seven of Swords
shortMeaning: Calculated cunning and strategic retreat require stealth — but beware the cost of deception to your soul.
reversedMeaning: Lies and deceptions unravel as the conscience awakens or the truth is dramatically brought to light.

rws.scene: A man creeps away from a camp of tents carrying five swords by the blades, two still planted behind him, looking back over his shoulder.
symbols: carrying the swords by the blades — a clever plan that cuts the hands
two left behind — the escape is incomplete
glancing back — he expects to be caught

name: Eight of Swords
shortMeaning: The blindfold and bindings are of your own mind — the path out exists if you're brave enough to look.
reversedMeaning: The blindfold finally falls away, revealing the freedom that was available to you all along.

rws.scene: A bound and blindfolded woman stands in mud among eight swords planted around her, a castle on the hill behind, the swords leaving a clear gap in front.
symbols: the gap in the swords — the way out is open and unseen
loose bindings — the restraint would not survive a real struggle
the castle above — whoever set this is elsewhere, not guarding her

name: Nine of Swords
shortMeaning: The darkest hour of the mind where midnight fears loom largest — speak your fears to dissolve their power.
reversedMeaning: After sitting with the nightmare, a turn toward hope and community offers genuine relief from mental anguish.

rws.scene: A person sits up in bed with their face in their hands, nine swords mounted on the black wall behind, the quilt embroidered with roses and zodiac signs.
symbols: swords on the wall, not in the body — the dread is not yet fact
total darkness behind — this is the middle of the night, not the day
the patterned quilt — comfort within reach, unnoticed

name: Ten of Swords
shortMeaning: Rock bottom arrives with ten swords in the back — but the dawn breaks over the horizon, promising renewal.
reversedMeaning: Rising from rock bottom, survival instincts activate and the long journey of recovery begins at last.

rws.scene: A figure lies face down with ten swords in the back, under a black sky, calm water beside, a golden dawn breaking along the horizon.
symbols: ten swords — theatrically excessive, the worst already complete
the dawn on the horizon — the sky is already turning
still water — the storm is spent

name: Page of Swords
shortMeaning: Sharp-eyed and quick-witted, you cut through with swift questions and keen observational energy.
reversedMeaning: Quick mind without wisdom becomes sharp-tongued and tactless, cutting where it should illuminate.

rws.scene: A youth stands braced on rough ground holding a sword up in both hands, looking back over one shoulder, hair and clouds driven by wind, birds overhead.
symbols: looking back while holding the sword up — vigilance verging on suspicion
the wind — restless mental energy with nowhere to settle
both hands on the hilt — more grip than skill

name: Knight of Swords
shortMeaning: Charge forward with decisive clarity and fearless ambition — the direct path demands your full commitment.
reversedMeaning: Reckless speed and abrasive directness alienate allies and scatter the focused energy needed for success.

rws.scene: A knight charges at full gallop with sword raised, cloak and mane streaming, trees bent double behind him.
symbols: full gallop — speed with no stopping distance
the storm-bent trees — the surroundings cannot absorb this pace
sword already raised — argument before arrival

name: Queen of Swords
shortMeaning: Clear-eyed and impartial, you wield the sword of truth with the earned wisdom of hard experience.
reversedMeaning: Pain hardens into cruelty and bitterness, using sharp intellect as a weapon rather than a guide.

rws.scene: A stern queen sits on a throne carved with a sylph and butterflies, an upright sword in one hand, the other hand open and extended, clouds beneath her.
symbols: the open hand — invitation and honesty offered together
the upright sword — clarity that has already cost her something
above the clouds — perspective bought by distance

name: King of Swords
shortMeaning: Rule with the combined powers of clear intellect and moral authority, cutting through noise to just truth.
reversedMeaning: Intellectual authority becomes tyrannical when detached from compassion and bent toward manipulation.

rws.scene: A king faces forward on a throne carved with butterflies and crescent moons, an upright sword tilted slightly, clouds massing behind.
symbols: facing straight ahead — judgement without evasion
the slight tilt of the sword — the verdict is not perfectly impartial
butterflies on the throne — the mind remembers it once transformed

name: Ace of Pentacles
shortMeaning: A golden coin of opportunity is offered — plant this seed of material abundance with careful intention.
reversedMeaning: A financial opportunity slips away through poor planning or a scarcity mindset that repels abundance.

goldenDawn.gdTitle: Root of the Powers of Earth

rws.scene: A hand from a cloud holds out a large pentacle above a walled garden of white lilies, an arched gate opening onto mountains.
symbols: the garden gate — an opening onto something you would have to walk to
lilies, cultivated — this abundance is tended, not wild
the coin held flat — offered, and heavy

name: Two of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Juggle life's demands with graceful adaptability — the dance of balance keeps all priorities in motion.
reversedMeaning: Too many balls in the air begins to show — disorganization and overwhelm signal the need to reprioritize.

rws.scene: A young man dances balancing two pentacles inside a looping infinity ribbon, two ships riding high waves behind him.
symbols: the infinity ribbon — juggling that could continue indefinitely
the ships on rough swell — conditions are not calm underneath
dancing, not straining — competence that looks like play

name: Three of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Master craftspeople collaborate in sacred space — excellence is built through skilled and willing teamwork.
reversedMeaning: Team misalignment or poor communication undermines the quality of the work being constructed together.

rws.scene: A sculptor stands on a bench in a cathedral showing his carving to a monk and a nobleman holding architectural plans.
symbols: three people, three roles — craft, vision and funding in one room
the sculptor raised on a bench — the maker's word carries here
an unfinished cathedral — long work, early stage

name: Four of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Holding tightly to resources brings security but risks clutching too hard, blocking the flow of abundance.
reversedMeaning: Hoarding from fear of scarcity paradoxically creates the poverty mindset that keeps abundance away.

rws.scene: A crowned figure grips one pentacle against his chest, balances another on his crown and pins two beneath his feet, a city behind him.
symbols: all four pentacles held down — nothing circulating
the pentacle on the crown — identity fused with holding on
the city at his back — he sits outside what he is guarding against

name: Five of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Out in the cold, struggling through lack — yet the warm light of support shines in the window above.
reversedMeaning: A period of lack begins to ease as inner resources and available support are finally noticed and received.

rws.scene: Two beggars pass through snow beneath a lit stained-glass window — one on crutches, one barefoot and bandaged.
symbols: the lit window right above them — help present and unseen
two of them together — hardship shared, not solitary
passing by, not stopping — they do not think it is for them

name: Six of Pentacles
shortMeaning: The balanced scales of giving and receiving create a harmonious flow of abundance through your world.
reversedMeaning: Generosity with strings attached creates unhealthy power dynamics rather than genuine reciprocal exchange.

rws.scene: A merchant holds level scales in one hand while dropping coins into the hands of two kneeling beggars.
symbols: the scales — generosity that is being measured
one gives, two kneel — the exchange is not between equals
open palms below — receiving requires a posture

name: Seven of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Pause over your harvest and assess — patient tending of this crop will yield the rich reward you seek.
reversedMeaning: Impatience and poor investment choices rob the garden of the patient tending it needs to truly flourish.

rws.scene: A young man leans on a hoe, looking at seven pentacles growing on a leafy bush.
symbols: leaning on the tool — a deliberate pause in the middle of labour
fruit on the vine, unpicked — grown but not yet gathered
his gaze on the crop — assessment, and some doubt

name: Eight of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Dedicated practice and devoted craftsmanship turn raw talent into mastery one deliberate repetition at a time.
reversedMeaning: Cutting corners or perfectionism that prevents completion undermines the mastery you're striving toward.

rws.scene: A craftsman at a bench carves a pentacle, six finished ones mounted on a post beside him and one at his feet, a town in the distance.
symbols: six already hung up — repetition that has become skill
the distant town — he has withdrawn from company to work
head down at the bench — absorbed, not performing

name: Nine of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Standing in your abundant garden, you enjoy the luxurious fruits of your self-made independence and success.
reversedMeaning: Material comfort without inner contentment reveals unresolved self-worth issues beneath the surface.

rws.scene: A richly dressed woman stands alone in a walled vineyard with a hooded falcon on her gloved hand, a snail on the ground beside her.
symbols: the hooded falcon — appetite trained and kept still
the walled garden — plenty, and enclosure
the snail — slow accumulation, carrying its own house

name: Ten of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Enduring wealth, family legacy, and the satisfaction of lasting success built across generations.
reversedMeaning: Family conflict or short-sighted choices erode the lasting legacy that should be passed forward.

rws.scene: An old man with two dogs sits at an archway while a couple and a child stand nearby, ten pentacles arranged across the scene in the pattern of the Tree of Life.
symbols: three generations in one frame — wealth measured across time
the pentacles in the Tree of Life pattern — the material fully worked out
the old man unnoticed by the others — the founder already in the background

name: Page of Pentacles
shortMeaning: A student of the material world gazes at a golden pentacle, ready to learn and build something lasting.
reversedMeaning: Procrastination and lack of focus delay the manifestation of the practical ambitions you hold.

rws.scene: A youth stands in a flowering field holding a pentacle aloft in both hands, absorbed in looking at it.
symbols: both hands and full attention on the coin — study before spending
the flowering field — fertile ground, nothing built yet
standing still — the plan has not moved yet

name: Knight of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Slow, steady, and supremely reliable, this knight shows that methodical determination achieves lasting goals.
reversedMeaning: Complacency and boredom stagnate a knight whose dependability has curdled into stubborn inflexibility.

rws.scene: An armoured knight sits motionless on a heavy black horse holding out a pentacle, a ploughed field behind him.
symbols: the horse standing still — the only stationary knight in the deck
the ploughed field — work already done, methodically
the pentacle held out flat — steady, unglamorous reliability

name: Queen of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Earthly wisdom and nurturing warmth create a sanctuary of abundance, comfort, and practical security.
reversedMeaning: Anxiety around financial security leads to smothering those in your care or neglecting your own needs.

rws.scene: A queen sits on a throne carved with fruit and goats' heads, cradling a pentacle in her lap and gazing down at it, roses overhead and a rabbit at her feet.
symbols: the coin cradled like something living — resources treated as care
the rabbit — fertility, and quick unsentimental instinct
her gaze down, not out — attention to what is actually in her hands

name: King of Pentacles
shortMeaning: Master of the material world, your disciplined leadership builds enduring wealth and rock-solid security.
reversedMeaning: Material success corrupts into greed and stubbornness, sacrificing integrity for the protection of wealth.

rws.scene: A king sits on a bull-carved throne in a robe patterned with grapevines, one hand on a pentacle, a castle and vines behind him.
symbols: grapes on the robe — wealth that grew rather than was seized
the bull throne — stubborn, fertile, immovable
the castle behind — the estate is built; this is stewardship now
